To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the site-selectivity of cyclic AMP ( cAMP) analogues in binding to the cyclic AMP receptor protein is a determinant of growth regulatory activity.
the site-selectivity of cyclic AMP analogues, which bind to the RII c-AMP receptor protein with a high affinity, is a key factor for growth regulation of breast and colon cancer cells.
site-selective c AMP analogues are manyfold more potent inhibitors of human cancer cell growth than previously studied analogs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of cAMP-mediated control of tumor growth.
the mechanism of cyclic nucleotide (cyclic AMP) mediated growth inhibition of human breast cancer cells.
the development of new strategies for the treatment of human cancer, using cAMP analogues as a new type of antineoplastic agent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

site-selective analogs of cAMP are potent growth inhibitors of human breast and colon cancer cell lines, and the growth inhibition is mediated by the cAMP receptor, the RII subunit of cAmp-dependent protein kinase type-II.
site-selective c AMP analogues provide a new and promising approach to the control of human breast and colon cancer growth.

the growth of breast cancer cell lines is inhibited by site-selective c-AMP analogues, that this inhibition is mediated by the cAMP receptor, and that the inhibition parallels the augmentation of the R-II cAMP receptor protein and the reduction in p21ras protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

cAMP receptor protein is the target for growth control of breast and colon cancer cells, and that the site-selectivity of cAMP analogues provides a new physiological means for the control of tumor growth.
the RII cAMPR protein is a key regulator in controlling the growth of breast, colon, and other human cancers.
the RII c AMP receptor protein, the target of site-selective c AMP analogues, plays a key role in the control of tumor growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
site-selective c-AMP analogues are potent growth inhibitors of human breast cancer cell line, MCF-7.
cAMP analogues are effective inhibitors of growth of breast cancer cell lines and that these analogues are also effective in colon cancer cell lines.
the RII c-AMP receptor protein is a target for cancer therapy.
